resources.string: Come back when you add more data!

The bars rise from the floor, one a week. The line is the share of firm or partly mornings in the same week against your own average over these weeks: above the middle line when it was higher, below when it was lower. They show what was recorded in the same weeks, not what caused what.

plurals.name: intimate_charts_week_rule
plurals.item: A week counts once %1$d of its mornings was answered; a week with fewer leaves a gap in the line, never a zero.
A week counts once %1$d of its mornings were answered; a week with fewer leaves a gap in the line, never a zero.

plurals.name: intimate_charts_mean_rule
plurals.item: A week’s bar is the mean of the days with a reading and needs %1$d of them; a week with fewer has no bar.
A week’s bar is the mean of the days with a reading and needs %1$d of them; a week with fewer has no bar.

plurals.name: intimate_charts_show_rule
plurals.item: The chart appears once %1$d week has enough to show.
The chart appears once %1$d weeks have enough to show.

resources.string: One standard drink is %1$s of pure alcohol. For drinks, a day with a reading is a day with anything kept by hand, and the mean is scaled to seven days: a day with nothing written is not a day without a drink.
Acts each week, partnered and solo. A week in which you wrote nothing down yourself breaks both lines: it is not a week without acts.
A dot on a line: a week with “%1$s” ticked on that kind of act.
A dash on a line: a week with “%1$s” ticked on that kind of act.
The mornings have charts of their own: they are one answer a day from a separate check-in, not a count of acts, and drawn on these axes they would read as caused by them.

plurals.name: intimate_charts_spoken
plurals.item: %1$s, week by week over the last %2$d week. %3$s
